metadata.title: IoT Device Core

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for defining, classifying, and governing Internet of Things devices and their trust boundaries.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Internet of Things (IoT), embedded systems, and edge‑connected device technologies.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Pattern establishing the scope, trust boundaries, and baseline assumptions for IoT devices.

props.name: threat-framework
props.remarks: IoT device context for understanding attacker behavior targeting exposed or unmanaged devices.

props.name: attack-techniques
props.remarks: Relevant ATT&CK tactics include Initial Access, Lateral Movement, and Impact affecting IoT environments.

props.name: defense-framework
props.remarks: IoT core governance aligns with defensive techniques for asset visibility and boundary definition.

props.name: defensive-techniques
props.remarks: Defensive techniques supporting baseline IoT device trust and risk reduction.

metadata.remarks: Device Core defines what constitutes an IoT device, the baseline assumptions under which it operates, and the physical, network, and logical trust boundaries that constrain it. Control realization is expressed at the capability level using NIST IoT Core Baseline guidance.

components.title: Device Identification and Classification
components.description: Identification and classification of IoT devices by type, role, capability, and risk.

implemented-requirements.remarks: IoT devices are uniquely identifiable and categorized based on function, deployment, and risk.

components.title: Device Trust Boundaries
components.description: Definition of physical, logical, and network boundaries separating IoT devices from other systems.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Trust boundaries are defined to limit the blast radius of compromised IoT devices.

components.title: Baseline Device Assumptions
components.description: Documentation of baseline assumptions regarding device capability, connectivity, updateability, and exposure.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Baseline security and operational assumptions are defined for IoT devices based on their constraints.
